tagline: An opening is a relation between time and judgment
definition: The fitting, opportune, or decisive moment for an action, understood through the demands of a situation rather than solely through measured duration; a central concern in rhetoric and practical judgment.
etymology: From Greek kairos, an appropriate time, occasion, or critical point; its deeper derivation is disputed and should not be invented.

sections.heading: More than clock time
sections.text: A speech can be accurate and eloquent yet arrive when its audience cannot use it. Kairos concerns the fitting moment and manner of intervention within circumstances. The relevant measure is not merely how many seconds have elapsed, but what this situation now makes possible or necessary.

sections.heading: Opportunity demands interpretation
sections.text: No visible opening announces its own ethical meaning. A moment may be advantageous for manipulation as readily as for correction or care. Kairos therefore requires judgment about purpose, audience, consequences, and responsibility, rather than celebrating opportunism or treating successful timing as proof that an action was right.

sections.heading: The rhetorical encounter
sections.text: A speaker must decide when to interrupt, when to wait, which evidence an audience needs, and what form an appeal should take. These choices connect timing to appropriateness. The concept describes a situated practice of response, not a universal formula for turning any argument into persuasion.

sections.heading: The familiar contrast has limits
sections.text: Kairos is often contrasted with chronos, measured or sequential time. That distinction helps introduce the topic, but ancient usages resist a perfectly tidy division. A fitting moment can have a measurable duration; what matters is that its significance cannot be exhausted by reporting that duration alone.

literary: Between the wave's decision and its breaking, she placed the little boat, and all the hours that had refused her suddenly narrowed into one welcoming width of water.
art_caption: A narrow passage through two interrupted wheels admits one trajectory: opportunity depends on alignment as well as motion.
